title: A run's status must not collapse pipeline stages the backend already distinguishes
requirement: Where a Clank's backend already models a run as passing through distinct pipeline stages (a stage field, a stage-ordered ledger, or an equivalent structured record of what point execution reached), the primary run surface MUST NOT present a single terminal status (e.g. FAILED) in a way that erases a distinction the backend itself already tracks, when that distinction would materially change what an operator should do next. The primary run surface does not need to render every stage inline, but it MUST visibly indicate that deeper stage information exists and provide a direct, discoverable path to it — inline stage columns, an expandable row, a linked detail drawer, or a linked run-detail page all satisfy this. A page that technically contains the stage data but is not linked from, or indicated on, the primary run surface (an operator would have to already know the URL or guess) does NOT satisfy this — it is technically present but operationally absent.
rationale: Near-universal pattern across the fleet: almost every surveyed Clank records one terminal status per run (RUNNING/SUCCESS/FAILED or similar) with aggregate counters, and none except watch-clank model true pipeline-stage data at all. Where stage data does exist — watch-clank's PipelineLedger, with an explicit stage_order (discovery -> fetch -> snapshot_storage -> parsing -> normalization -> identity_resolution -> observation_creation -> family_candidate_assignment) — it is reachable only via non-nav-linked per-item drill-down pages (/watches/{id}, /correlation/{id}), not from the primary Runs page, which shows only one status badge plus funnel counts. This rule is scoped narrowly (only where stage data already exists) specifically because most Clanks have no stage model to expose, and manufacturing one would be a backend change, not a UI standard.
forbidden: Inventing or requiring new backend stage-tracking where none currently exists (out of scope for this UI standard)
A primary run list that shows one undifferentiated FAILED for runs that failed at materially different points, when the backend can already tell the difference
Stage-level data existing on some page in the codebase with no link, indicator, or discoverable path to it from the primary run surface
acceptance: If stage-level data exists in the backend for a run, the primary run surface visibly indicates it exists (not silently omits it) and provides a direct, clickable path to it
Acceptable forms: inline stage columns, an expandable row, a linked detail drawer, or a linked run-detail page — an unlinked/undiscoverable route does not count
The primary run list does not present one undifferentiated terminal status where the backend already distinguishes materially different failure points

evidence.summary: PipelineLedger with an explicit stage_order list — real stage data exists in the fleet's reference implementation.
Primary Runs page shows only a single status badge and funnel counts; stage detail is reachable only via drill-down pages not linked from primary nav.

evidence.source: oem-radar/src/oem_radar/dashboard/data.py:212-228; tablet-clank/pipeline/__init__.py:11,48-56; feature-phone-clank (collector_runs schema); chinese-tech-wire/database/models.py:559-573; korean-tech-wire/dashboard.py:59-90; smartwatch-clank (runs table, healthy-only column); smartphone-clank/database/models.py:145-160; semiconductor-intelligence/semi_intel/pipeline/service.py:131,271
evidence.summary: Every other surveyed Clank has no true stage model — one terminal status plus aggregate counters is the norm, sometimes with a failure-type breakdown (parse vs. request error counts) but not a stage sequence.

notes: RATIFIED 2026-08-30 by Operator Ratification Decision 002 (decisions/0004-operator-ratification-decision-002.md), resolving the open strictness question against the permissive reading. Version 2: requirement/acceptance rewritten to require the primary run surface to visibly indicate that deeper stage data exists and provide a direct path to it — an unlinked/undiscoverable page does not satisfy this. Under this stricter reading, watch-clank's current implementation (stage data reachable only via /watches/{id} and /correlation/{id}, not linked from or indicated on the primary Runs page) does NOT conform and is a live remediation-relevant example, not an exception.
